title: Consent to take part in this study
studyTitle: FocusGuard: An Analysis of Real-Time Visual Distraction Detection Through Webcam-Based Gaze and Facial Landmark Tracking Using Heuristic and Decision Trees
_note: Summary text below is paraphrased FROM the attached ISEF form so the on-screen wording and the signed PDF cannot drift apart. If you edit the PDF, edit these lines and bump `version` — the version string is stored with every consent receipt, so revising the form without bumping it makes older receipts unattributable.
summary: Purpose: to test whether FocusGuard can use a regular computer webcam to detect signs of distraction, such as looking away from the screen or looking at a phone, and whether alerts help you focus.
You will complete timed computer tasks while FocusGuard uses your webcam to track your head position and eye movements.
Time required: about 40-45 minutes, including setup, testing, and breaks.
Possible risks: eye strain from using a computer, frustration from alerts or automatic pauses, and privacy concerns from using a webcam. You can take breaks or stop at any time.
Benefits: there may be no direct benefit to you. The results could help show whether FocusGuard can detect visual distractions and help people reduce phone use while working.

Confidentiality: you are given a code instead of your name. Your webcam video never leaves this device - no image, video, or screenshot is uploaded or stored. The page turns each frame into a few numbers, such as how far your head is turned, and then discards the frame. Only those numbers, your task scores, and your code are sent to the researcher.
Participation is completely voluntary. If you decide not to take part there will be no negative consequences, and you may stop at any time or skip any question.
statements: I have read and understand the information above and the attached consent form.
I understand my webcam video stays on this device and is never uploaded.
I understand participation is voluntary and I can stop at any time without giving a reason.
I freely give my consent or assent to participate, or permission for my child to participate.
